annotations.title: Get an Old Norse inflection table

description:
Fetch the full declension (nominals) or conjugation (verbs — active AND
mediopassive) tables for a lemma identified by a search result's inflection
handle (entry_id + word_class). Use this only when a search ran without
inline forms or left a match un-expanded — a default search already returns
each match's table inline. Returns Markdown plus the table as
structuredContent with the shape {"result": <paradigm>} per the declared
outputSchema — switch on result.category ('nominal' | 'verbal' |
'not_found') before reading the body. Content from en.wiktionary.org
(CC BY-SA 4.0).

entry_id.description: The Wiktionary page title (the lemma) from a search result's inflection handle, e.g. 'maðr', 'kasta'.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

word_class.description: The part-of-speech section from a search result's inflection handle, e.g. 'verb', 'noun', 'adjective'.
word_class.title: Word Class

name: norse_get_inflections

NorseNominalParadigm.description:
Declension of a noun/adjective/etc.: case key → {singular, plural}.

Noun tables split by definiteness, folded into the key as a prefix:
'indefinite nominative', 'definite genitive'. Adjective tables split by gender
(suffixed: 'nominative feminine') and come one per declension class and degree,
folded in as a caption-derived prefix: 'strong nominative feminine',
'weak superlative accusative neuter', 'comparative dative masculine'.
``category`` discriminates this from the verbal and not-found shapes — switch
on it before reading the body.

cases.description: Case key (lower-case: 'nominative', 'genitive', …; nouns prefix the definiteness — 'indefinite nominative'; adjectives prefix the caption-derived declension class/degree and suffix the gender — 'strong nominative feminine') → its singular/plural forms, in table order.
cases.title: Cases

NorseNumberForms.description:
A declension cell: the two number forms of one case key. Forms are verbatim
normalized Old Norse; alternates stay comma-separated as Wiktionary renders
them. A number the table doesn't give (defective paradigms) is an empty
string.
NorseNumberForms.title: NorseNumberForms

NorseVerbalParadigm.description:
Conjugation of a verb, grouped the way Wiktionary's tables are: finite cells
keyed by mood and tense → person-and-number → form, plus the non-finite forms
(infinitive and the participles). The mediopassive voice renders as its own
table and its keys carry a 'mediopassive ' prefix; active keys are bare.

finite.description: Mood and tense (lower-case: 'indicative present', 'subjunctive past', 'imperative present'; the mediopassive table's keys are prefixed — 'mediopassive indicative past') → person and number ('first singular' … 'third plural') → the form. Alternates are comma-separated; an em-dash cell (no such form) is omitted.
finite.title: Finite

nonfinite.description: Non-finite form ('infinitive', 'present participle', 'past participle'; mediopassive-prefixed for that voice) → {'form': <the form>}.
nonfinite.title: Nonfinite

No inflection table for this page/POS (no Old Norse section, no table, or
the page doesn't exist). ``found`` is False and there is no body.
